subtype: Approach: sets the bar too low on an important decision [Pitfall]
passage: Mohit, before you sign anything on Saturday, let me tell you about my first flat. I'm Ankita, and at twenty-four I saw one flat, and it had a bed, a working tap and a rent I could afford. I had decided beforehand that it only needed to be 'fine', the way I choose a phone case. So I said yes that evening. I never read the lease properly, and I never travelled the route to work at eight in the morning. My cousin Divya visited in the third month and asked how I survived the trip. It took ninety minutes with two changes, and the lease held my deposit for a year. I stayed, tired, until the year ended. A phone case I could replace; a year I couldn't.

qa.q: How long did the commute take?
qa.a: The commute took ninety minutes with two changes.

qa.q: What did Ankita feel while staying until the year ended?
qa.a: Ankita felt tired and probably regretful, stuck with a choice made too quickly.

qa.q: Which choice caused most of the trouble, and what could have been done differently?
qa.a: Saying yes that evening without reading the lease or travelling the route caused it, and both checks could have been done before signing.

qa.q: How might Divya have seen Ankita's daily trip?
qa.a: Divya was likely worried and surprised by the long trip, which is why Divya asked how Ankita survived it.

grounding: Shows a young professional accepting the first flat that meets basic needs without checking the lease or the commute, a standard that suits a cheap purchase but not a year-long commitment.
